hook_patterns: Start with a relatable everyday problem then flip it with a surprising psychological twist
Pose a bold, curiosity‑inducing question in the title that promises a simple, visual answer
Use rapid, joke‑filled pacing that builds to an aha moment at the end
todays_angle: Show how the Spotlight Effect makes Leo think everyone noticed his embarrassing sneeze, while Mia reveals why it’s just his brain over‑reacting.
ideas: Leo sneezes loudly in a quiet library; Mia narrates the Spotlight Effect with exaggerated thought bubbles showing imagined stares.
Leo and Mia swap roles: Leo pretends to ignore a noisy roommate, Mia explains the Ben Franklin effect as they end up liking each other more for the favor.
A split‑screen shows Leo craving pizza vs. his diet plan; Mia uses fast cuts to illustrate cognitive dissonance and the humor of inner conflict.
avoid: Overused overthinking vs. motivation vs. discipline tropes
Clickbait crime‑story hooks like "Bank robber lemon juice" that don’t tie to psychology
